Please solve this issue: The Tokyo office wants Fizzy in Japanese, upstream says internationalization
is never coming, so it lands on us.

Make the app speak more than one language. Japanese has to ship complete: a
person who chose Japanese gets every screen and every email in Japanese,
dates included. Nothing readable may stay hardcoded English — the text a
screen reader announces is readable too.

Opening any page with `?locale=ja` switches that person to Japanese, and the
choice sticks: for the rest of their session, and again the next time they
sign in from a clean browser. A locale we don't offer (`?locale=xx`) never
breaks a page — it just doesn't switch anything.

People who never chose anything must not notice any of this
happened: their pages keep rendering exactly the English they render today.
One exception: the static error pages are served without knowing who is
looking, so render those in both languages.

The rich-text editor ships its own strings inside its JavaScript package.
Leave those alone.

  "output": "# Fizzy

Guidance for AI coding agents working with this repository.

Fizzy is a kanban-style project management and issue tracker: cards move across columns on boards, with comments, mentions, and assignments.

## Deploy

Default branch: `main`

Self-hosted deploys run Kamal against `config/deploy.yml` — see `docs/kamal-deployment.md`.

## SaaS mode

For local agent work, `tmp/saas.txt` is the checkout-level SaaS switch used by `bin/setup`. When present, read `saas/AGENTS.md` before continuing. Otherwise, do not apply its instructions.

## Architecture Overview

### Multi-Tenancy (URL-Based)

Fizzy uses **URL path-based multi-tenancy**:
- Accounts have a unique decimal `external_account_id` used in URL prefixes
- URLs are prefixed: `/{account_id}/boards/...`
- Middleware (`AccountSlug::Extractor`) extracts the account ID from the URL and sets `Current.account`
- The slug is moved from `PATH_INFO` to `SCRIPT_NAME`, making Rails think it's "mounted" at that path
- Tenant-scoped domain records are account-isolated; global identity, session, and authentication records are exceptions
- Background jobs automatically serialize and restore account context

**Key insight**: This architecture allows multi-tenancy without subdomains or separate databases, making local development and testing simpler.

### Authentication & Authorization

Passwordless magic link authentication. A global `Identity` (email-based) can have `Users` in multiple Accounts, so an email is not a single account membership. Users have roles: owner, admin, member, system. Board-level access control via `Access` records.

### Entropy System

Cards automatically "postpone" (move to "not now") after inactivity:
- Account-level default entropy period
- Board-level entropy override
- Prevents endless todo lists from accumulating
- Configurable via Account/Board settings

### UUID Primary Keys

All tables use UUIDs (UUIDv7 format, base36-encoded as 25-char strings):
- Custom fixture UUID generation maintains deterministic ordering for tests
- Fixtures are always "older" than runtime records
- `.first`/`.last` work correctly in tests

### Background Jobs (Solid Queue)

Database-backed job queue (no Redis):
- Custom `FizzyActiveJobExtensions` prepended to ActiveJob
- Jobs automatically capture/restore `Current.account`
- Mission Control::Jobs for monitoring

Recurring tasks are declared in `config/recurring.yml`.

### Sharded Full-Text Search

Full-text search runs in the database, not Elasticsearch. On MySQL it is sharded 16 ways by CRC32 of the account ID (`Search::Record::Trilogy`); on SQLite it is a single FTS5 index (`Search::Record::SQLite`). Don't assume the sharded shape when working under SQLite. Models in `app/models/search/`.

### Imports and exports

Allow people to move between OSS and SAAS Fizzy instances:
- Exports/Imports can be written to/read from local or S3 storage depending on the config of the instance (both must be supported)
- Must be able to handle very large ZIP files (500+GB)
- Models in `app/models/account/data_transfer/`, `app/models/zip_file`

## Coding style

Before editing or reviewing code, read STYLE.md.
# Fizzy

This is the source code of [Fizzy](https://fizzy.do/), the Kanban tracking tool for issues and ideas by [37signals](https://37signals.com).


## Running your own Fizzy instance

If you want to run your own Fizzy instance, but don't need to change its code, you can use our pre-built Docker image.
You'll need access to a server on which you can run Docker, and you'll need to configure some options to customize your installation.

You can find the details of how to do a Docker-based deployment in our [Docker deployment guide](docs/docker-deployment.md).

If you want more flexibility to customize your Fizzy installation by changing its code, and deploy those changes to your server, then we recommend you deploy Fizzy with Kamal. You can find a complete walkthrough of doing that in our [Kamal deployment guide](docs/kamal-deployment.md).


## Development

You are welcome -- and encouraged -- to modify Fizzy to your liking.
Please see our [Development guide](docs/development.md) for how to get Fizzy set up for local development.


## Contributing

We welcome contributions! Please read our [style guide](STYLE.md) before submitting code.


## License

Fizzy is released under the [O'Saasy License](LICENSE.md).
# How to contribute to Fizzy

Fizzy uses GitHub
[discussions](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/discussions) to track
feature requests and questions, rather than [the issue
tracker](https://github.com/basecamp/fizzy/issues). If you're considering
opening an issue or pull request, please open a discussion instead.

Whenever a discussion leads to an actionable and well-understood task, we'll
move it to the issue tracker where it can be worked on.

This is a little different than how some other projects work, but it makes it
easier for us to triage and prioritise the work. It also means that the open
issues all represent agreed-upon tasks that are either being worked on, or are
ready to be worked on.

This should also make it easier to see what's in progress, and to find
something to work on if you'd like to do so.

## What this means in practice

### If you'd like to contribute to the code...

1. If you're interested in working on one of the open issues, please do! We are
   grateful for the help!
2. You'll want to make sure someone else isn't already working on the same
   issue. If they are, it will be tagged "in progress" and/or it should be clear
   from the comments. When in doubt, you can always comment on the issue to ask.
3. Similarly, if you need any help or guidance on the issue, please comment on
   the issue as you go, and we'll do our best to help.
4. When you have something ready for review or collaboration, open a PR.

### If you've found a bug...

1. If you don't have steps to reproduce the problem, or you're not certain it's a
   bug, open a discussion.
2. If you have steps to reproduce, open an issue.

### If you have an idea for a feature...

1. Open a discussion.

### If you have a question, or are having trouble with configuration...

1. Open a discussion.

Hopefully this process makes it easier for everyone to be involved. Thanks for
helping! ❤️

CLAUDE.md
@../AGENTS.md
"
}

  "output": "
# Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

This is because guard clauses can be hard to read, especially when they are nested.

As an exception, we sometimes use guard clauses to return early from a method:

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

## Methods ordering

We order methods in classes in the following order:

1. `class` methods
2. `public` methods with `initialize` at the top.
3. `private` methods

## Invocation order

We order methods vertically based on their invocation order. This helps us to understand the flow of the code.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    method_1
    method_2
  end

  private
    def method_1
      method_1_1
      method_1_2
    end
  
    def method_1_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_1_2
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2
      method_2_1
      method_2_2
    end
  
    def method_2_1
      # ...
    end
  
    def method_2_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

## To bang or not to bang

Should I call a method `do_something` or `do_something!`?

As a general rule, we only use `!` for methods that have a correspondent counterpart without `!`. In particular, we don’t use `!` to flag destructive actions. There are plenty of destructive methods in Ruby and Rails that do not end with `!`.

## Visibility modifiers

We don't add a newline under visibility modifiers, and we indent the content under them.

```ruby
class SomeClass
  def some_method
    # ...
  end

  private
    def some_private_method_1
      # ...
    end

    def some_private_method_2
      # ...
    end
end
```

If a module only has private methods, we mark it `private` at the top and add an extra new line after but don't indent.

```ruby
module SomeModule
  private
  
  def some_private_method
    # ...
  end
end
```

## CRUD controllers

We model web endpoints as CRUD operations on resources (REST). When an action doesn't map cleanly to a standard CRUD verb, we introduce a new resource rather than adding custom actions.

```ruby
# Bad
resources :cards do
  post :close
  post :reopen
end

# Good
resources :cards do
  resource :closure
end
```

## Controller and model interactions

In general, we favor a [vanilla Rails](https://dev.37signals.com/vanilla-rails-is-plenty/) approach with thin controllers directly invoking a rich domain model. We don't use services or other artifacts to connect the two.

Invoking plain Active Record operations is totally fine:

```ruby
class Cards::CommentsController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @comment = @card.comments.create!(comment_params)
  end
end
```

For more complex behavior, we prefer clear, intention-revealing model APIs that controllers call directly:

```ruby
class Cards::GoldnessesController < ApplicationController
  def create
    @card.gild
  end
end
```

When justified, it is fine to use services or form objects, but don't treat those as special artifacts:

```ruby
Signup.new(email_address: email_address).create_identity
```

## Run async operations in jobs

As a general rule, we write shallow job classes that delegate the logic itself to domain models:

* We typically use the suffix `_later` to flag methods that enqueue a job.
* A common scenario is having a model class that enqueues a job that, when executed, invokes some method in that same class. In this case, we use the suffix `_now` for the regular synchronous method.

```ruby
  included do

  end

  def relay_later
    Event::RelayJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def relay_now
    # ...
  end
end

class Event::RelayJob < ApplicationJob
  def perform(event)
    event.relay_now
  end
end
```
# Fizzy SaaS

37signals' hosted Fizzy: billing, our production setup, our deploy destinations. Apply this only when SaaS mode is enabled — the root `AGENTS.md` has the check.

`saas:enable` is a prerequisite for deploying, not just for local development. Only under that flag does `bin/kamal` pass `-c` pointing at this gem's `config/deploy.yml`. # Style

We aim to write code that is a pleasure to read, and we have a lot of opinions about how to do it well. Writing great code is an essential part of our programming culture, and we deliberately set a high bar for every code change anyone contributes. We care about how code reads, how code looks, and how code makes you feel when you read it.

We love discussing code. If you have questions about how to write something, or if you detect some smell you are not quite sure how to solve, please ask away to other programmers. A Pull Request is a great way to do this.

When writing new code, unless you are very familiar with our approach, try to find similar code elsewhere to look for inspiration.

## Conditional returns

In general, we prefer to use expanded conditionals over guard clauses.

```ruby
# Bad
def todos_for_new_group
  ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
  return [] unless ids
  @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
end

# Good
def todos_for_new_group
  if ids = params.require(:todolist)[:todo_ids]
    @bucket.recordings.todos.find(ids.split(","))
  else
    []
  end
end
```

* When the return is right at the beginning of the method.
* When the main method body is not trivial and involves several lines of code.

```ruby
def after_recorded_as_commit(recording)
  return if recording.parent.was_created?

  if recording.was_created?
    broadcast_new_column(recording)
  else
    broadcast_column_change(recording)
  end
end
```

```ruby
      method_1_2
```

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    before_action do
      Current.http_method = request.method
      Current.request_id  = request.uuid
      Current.user_agent  = request.user_agent
      Current.ip_address  = request.ip
      Current.referrer    = request.referrer
    end
  end

module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    before_action :require_account # Checking and setting account must happen first
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :authenticated?
    helper_method :email_address_pending_authentication

    etag { Current.identity.id if authenticated? }

    include Authentication::ViaMagicLink, LoginHelper
  end

  class_methods do
    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      allow_unauthenticated_access **options
      before_action :redirect_authenticated_user, **options
    end

    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :resume_session, **options
      allow_unauthorized_access **options
    end

    def disallow_account_scope(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_account, **options
      before_action :redirect_tenanted_request, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def authenticated?
      Current.identity.present?
    end

    def require_account
      unless Current.account.present?
        redirect_to main_app.session_menu_path(script_name: nil)
      end
    end

    def require_authentication
      resume_session || authenticate_by_bearer_token || request_authentication
    end

    def resume_session
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        set_current_session session
      end
    end

    def find_session_by_cookie
      Session.find_signed(cookies.signed[:session_token])
    end

    def authenticate_by_bearer_token
      if request.authorization.to_s.include?("Bearer")
        if bearer_token_authenticatable_request?
          authenticate_or_request_with_http_token do |token|
            if identity = Identity.find_by_permissable_access_token(token, method: request.method)
              Current.identity = identity
            end
          end
        else
          request_http_token_authentication
        end
      end
    end

    def bearer_token_authenticatable_request?
      request.format.json?
    end

    def request_authentication
      if Current.account.present?
        session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      end

      redirect_to_login_url
    end

    def after_authentication_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || landing_url
    end

    def redirect_authenticated_user
      redirect_to main_app.root_url if authenticated?
    end

    def redirect_tenanted_request
      redirect_to main_app.root_url if Current.account.present?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(identity)
      identity.sessions.create!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        set_current_session session
      end
    end

    def set_current_session(session)
      Current.session = session
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.signed_id, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def terminate_session
      Current.session.destroy
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end

    def session_token
      cookies[:session_token]
    end
end

  included do
    before_action :require_account # Checking and setting account must happen first
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :authenticated?
    helper_method :email_address_pending_authentication

    etag { Current.identity.id if authenticated? }

    include Authentication::ViaMagicLink, LoginHelper
  end

  class_methods do
    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      allow_unauthenticated_access **options
      before_action :redirect_authenticated_user, **options
    end

    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :resume_session, **options
      allow_unauthorized_access **options
    end

    def disallow_account_scope(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_account, **options
      before_action :redirect_tenanted_request, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def authenticated?
      Current.identity.present?
    end

    def require_account
      unless Current.account.present?
        redirect_to main_app.session_menu_path(script_name: nil)
      end
    end

    def require_authentication
      resume_session || authenticate_by_bearer_token || request_authentication
    end

    def resume_session
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        set_current_session session
      end
    end

    def find_session_by_cookie
      Session.find_signed(cookies.signed[:session_token])
    end

    def authenticate_by_bearer_token
      if request.authorization.to_s.include?("Bearer")
        if bearer_token_authenticatable_request?
          authenticate_or_request_with_http_token do |token|
            if identity = Identity.find_by_permissable_access_token(token, method: request.method)
              Current.identity = identity
            end
          end
        else
          request_http_token_authentication
        end
      end
    end

    def bearer_token_authenticatable_request?
      request.format.json?
    end

    def request_authentication
      if Current.account.present?
        session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      end

      redirect_to_login_url
    end

    def after_authentication_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || landing_url
    end

    def redirect_authenticated_user
      redirect_to main_app.root_url if authenticated?
    end

    def redirect_tenanted_request
      redirect_to main_app.root_url if Current.account.present?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(identity)
      identity.sessions.create!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        set_current_session session
      end
    end

    def set_current_session(session)
      Current.session = session
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.signed_id, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def terminate_session
      Current.session.destroy
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end

    def session_token
      cookies[:session_token]
    end
end
module SetPlatform
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    helper_method :platform
  end

  private
    def platform
      @platform ||= ApplicationPlatform.new(cookies[:x_user_agent].presence || request.user_agent)
    end
end

mkdir -p /tmp/scan && cat > /tmp/scan/scan_erb.rb <<'EOF'
# Rough scanner: finds literal text nodes and readable attribute values in ERB templates.
ATTRS = /\b(aria-label|aria-description|aria-placeholder|aria-roledescription|aria-valuetext|title|alt|placeholder|label|summary|value|data-[a-z-]*(?:label|title|confirm|message|text|prompt|placeholder)[a-z-]*)=("([^"]*)"|'([^']*)')/
files = ARGV
total_text = 0
total_attr = 0
files.sort.each do |f|
  src = File.read(f)
  # strip erb tags but keep newlines
  stripped = src.gsub(/<%#.*?%>/m) { |m| "\n" * m.count("\n") }
                .gsub(/<%.*?%>/m) { |m| " " * 0 + ("\n" * m.count("\n")) }
  stripped.each_line.with_index(1) do |line, ln|
    # text nodes: between > and < with letters
    line.scan(/>([^<>]*)</).each do |(t)|
      tt = t.strip
      next if tt.empty?
      next unless tt =~ /[A-Za-z]{2,}/
      next if tt =~ /\A[a-z_\-]+\z/ # likely junk
      total_text += 1
      puts "#{f}:#{ln}: TEXT #{tt[0,120]}"
    end
    line.scan(ATTRS).each do |m|
      val = m[2][1..-2]
      next unless val =~ /[A-Za-z]{2,}/
      total_attr += 1
      puts "#{f}:#{ln}: ATTR #{m[0].split('=')[0]}=#{val[0,120]}"
    end
  end
end
STDERR.puts "text=#{total_text} attr=#{total_attr}"
EOF
cd /app && ruby /tmp/scan/scan_erb.rb $(find app/views -name "*.erb") > /tmp/scan/erb_hits.txt; tail -1 /tmp/scan/erb_hits.txt; wc -l /tmp/scan/erb_hits.txt; awk -F: '{print $1}' /tmp/scan/erb_hits.txt | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | wc -l

module FixturesTestHelper
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class_methods do
    def identify(label, column_type = :integer)
      if label.to_s.end_with?("_uuid")
        column_type = :uuid
        label = label.to_s.delete_suffix("_uuid")
      end

      # Rails passes :string for varchar columns, so handle both :uuid and :string
      return super(label, column_type) unless column_type.in?([ :uuid, :string ])
      generate_fixture_uuid(label)
    end

    private

    def generate_fixture_uuid(label)
      # Generate deterministic UUIDv7 for fixtures that sorts by fixture ID
      # This allows .first/.last to work as expected in tests
      # Use the same CRC32 algorithm as Rails' default fixture ID generation
      # so that UUIDs sort in the same order as integer IDs
      fixture_int = Zlib.crc32("fixtures/#{label}") % (2**30 - 1)

      # Translate the deterministic order into times in the past, so that records
      # created during test runs are also always newer than the fixtures.
      base_time = Time.utc(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
      timestamp = base_time + (fixture_int / 1000.0)

      uuid_v7_with_timestamp(timestamp, label)
    end

    def uuid_v7_with_timestamp(time, seed_string)
      # Generate UUIDv7 with custom timestamp and deterministic random bits
      # Format: 48-bit timestamp_ms | 12-bit sub_ms_precision | 4-bit version | 62-bit random

      time_ms = time.to_f * 1000
      timestamp_ms = time_ms.to_i

      # 48-bit timestamp (milliseconds since epoch)
      bytes = []
      bytes[0] = (timestamp_ms >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[1] = (timestamp_ms >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[2] = (timestamp_ms >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[3] = (timestamp_ms >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[4] = (timestamp_ms >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[5] = timestamp_ms & 0xff

      # Use the 12-bit rand_a field for sub-millisecond precision
      # Extract fractional milliseconds and convert to 12-bit value (0-4095)
      # This gives us ~0.244 microsecond precision
      frac_ms = time_ms - timestamp_ms
      sub_ms_precision = (frac_ms * 4096).to_i & 0xfff

      # Derive deterministic "random" bits from seed_string for the remaining random bits
      hash = Digest::MD5.hexdigest(seed_string)

      # 12-bit sub-ms precision + 4-bit version (0111 for v7)
      bytes[6] = ((sub_ms_precision >> 8) & 0x0f) | 0x70  # version 7
      bytes[7] = sub_ms_precision & 0xff

      # 2-bit variant (10) + 62-bit random
      rand_b = hash[3...19].to_i(16) & ((2**62) - 1)
      bytes[8] = ((rand_b >> 56) & 0x3f) | 0x80  # variant 10
      bytes[9] = (rand_b >> 48) & 0xff
      bytes[10] = (rand_b >> 40) & 0xff
      bytes[11] = (rand_b >> 32) & 0xff
      bytes[12] = (rand_b >> 24) & 0xff
      bytes[13] = (rand_b >> 16) & 0xff
      bytes[14] = (rand_b >> 8) & 0xff
      bytes[15] = rand_b & 0xff

      # Format as UUID string and convert to base36 (25 chars)
      uuid = "%02x%02x%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x-%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x%02x" % bytes
      ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid.hex_to_base36(uuid.delete("-"))
    end
  end

messages.content: I have enough fixture names to build a snapshot harness. It will sign in as a real user, render a broad set of pages and emails, and save normalized HTML so I can diff English output before and after my changes.

arguments.command:
mkdir -p /tmp/snap && cat > /tmp/snap/snap_test.rb <<'EOF'
require "/app/test/test_helper"

# Temporary snapshot harness (not part of the change). Dumps normalized HTML
# for a broad set of pages so English output can be diffed before/after.
class SnapshotTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  OUT = ENV.fetch("SNAP_DIR")

  def norm(body)
    body.gsub(/name="csrf-token" content="[^"]*"/, 'name="csrf-token" content="X"')
        .gsub(/authenticity_token" value="[^"]*"/, 'authenticity_token" value="X"')
        .gsub(/nonce="[^"]*"/, 'nonce="X"')
        .gsub(/content="[A-Za-z0-9+\/=_-]{40,}"/, 'content="X"')
        .gsub(/\b[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}\b/, "UUID")
  end

  def dump(name)
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(OUT)
    File.write(File.join(OUT, "#{name}.html"), "STATUS #{response.status}\n" + norm(response.body))
  end

  def get_as_user(name, path)
    get path
    dump(name)
  rescue => e
    File.write(File.join(OUT, "#{name}.html"), "ERROR #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
  end

  test "snapshot" do
    untenanted do
      get "/session/new"; dump "sessions_new"
      get "/signup/new"; dump "signup_new"
      get "/session/magic_link"; dump "magic_link_show"
      get "/session/menu"; dump "session_menu_anon"
      get "/join/nonexistent"; dump "join_bad"
    end

    sign_in_as :kevin
    b = boards(:writebook)
    c = cards(:logo)
    pages = {
      "root" => "/",
      "boards_new" => "/boards/new",
      "board_show" => "/boards/#{b.id}",
      "board_edit" => "/boards/#{b.id}/edit",
      "board_columns_new" => "/boards/#{b.id}/columns/new",
      "board_accesses" => "/boards/#{b.id}/accesses",
      "board_webhooks" => "/boards/#{b.id}/webhooks",
      "board_webhooks_new" => "/boards/#{b.id}/webhooks/new",
      "card_show" => "/cards/#{c.number}",
      "card_edit_board" => "/cards/#{c.number}/board/edit",
      "card_steps_new" => "/cards/#{c.number}/steps/new",
      "card_assignments_new" => "/cards/#{c.number}/assignments/new",
      "card_taggings_new" => "/cards/#{c.number}/taggings/new",
      "card_draft" => "/cards/#{c.number}/draft",
      "card_comments_edit" => "/cards/#{c.number}/comments/#{comments(:logo_1).id}/edit",
      "card_comment_show" => "/cards/#{c.number}/comments/#{comments(:logo_1).id}",
      "events" => "/events",
      "events_day" => "/events/days/#{Date.current.iso8601}",
      "activities" => "/activities",
      "notifications" => "/notifications",
      "notification_tray" => "/notifications/tray",
      "notifications_settings" => "/notifications/settings",
      "notifications_unsubscribe" => "/notifications/unsubscribe",
      "search" => "/search",
      "search_q" => "/search?q=logo",
      "tags" => "/tags",
      "filters_new" => "/filters/new",
      "my_identity" => "/my/identity",
      "my_access_tokens" => "/my/access_tokens",
      "my_access_tokens_new" => "/my/access_tokens/new",
      "my_passkeys" => "/my/passkeys",
      "my_pins" => "/my/pins",
      "my_menu" => "/my/menu",
      "account_settings" => "/account/settings",
      "account_join_code" => "/account/join_code",
      "account_join_code_edit" => "/account/join_code/edit",
      "account_entropy" => "/account/entropy/edit",
      "account_imports_new" => "/account/imports/new",
      "users_show" => "/users/#{users(:kevin).id}",
      "users_edit" => "/users/#{users(:kevin).id}/edit",
      "user_avatar" => "/users/#{users(:kevin).id}/avatar",
      "user_email_addresses_new" => "/users/#{users(:kevin).id}/email_addresses/new",
      "user_events" => "/users/#{users(:kevin).id}/events",
      "qr_codes" => "/qr_codes/new",
      "pwa_manifest" => "/manifest.json",
      "prompts_users" => "/prompts/users?board_id=#{b.id}",
      "prompts_cards" => "/prompts/cards",
      "prompts_commands" => "/prompts/cards",
      "cards_new_board" => "/boards/#{b.id}/cards",
      "public_board_missing" => "/public/boards/nope",
      "searches_queries" => "/searches/queries",
    }
    pages.each { |name, path| get_as_user(name, path) }

    # Emails
    magic = identities(:kevin).send(:magic_links).create!(purpose: "sign_in")
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(OUT)
    m = MagicLinkMailer.sign_in_instructions(magic)
    File.write(File.join(OUT, "mail_magic_link.txt"), m.subject + "\n---\n" + m.text_part.body.to_s + "\n---\n" + m.html_part.body.to_s)
  end
end
EOF

# Integrates the WebAuthn and Passkey subsystems into the Rails application.

# challenge endpoint route.
#
# == Configuration
#
#   # config/application.rb or config/initializers/passkeys.rb
#   config.action_pack.web_authn.default_creation_options = { attestation: :none }
#   config.action_pack.web_authn.default_request_options  = { user_verification: :required }
#   config.action_pack.web_authn.creation_challenge_expiration = 10.minutes
#   config.action_pack.web_authn.request_challenge_expiration = 5.minutes
#
#   config.action_pack.passkey.routes_prefix = "/rails/action_pack/passkey"
#   config.action_pack.passkey.draw_routes   = true
#
class ActionPack::Railtie < Rails::Railtie
  config.action_pack = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new unless config.respond_to?(:action_pack)

  config.action_pack.web_authn = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
  config.action_pack.web_authn.default_request_options = {}
  config.action_pack.web_authn.default_creation_options = {}
  config.action_pack.web_authn.creation_challenge_expiration = 10.minutes
  config.action_pack.web_authn.request_challenge_expiration = 5.minutes

  config.action_pack.passkey = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
  config.action_pack.passkey.parent_class_name = "ApplicationRecord"
  config.action_pack.passkey.routes_prefix = "/rails/action_pack/passkey"
  config.action_pack.passkey.draw_routes = true
  config.action_pack.passkey.challenge_url = nil

  initializer "action_pack.passkey.routes" do |app|
    passkey_config = config.action_pack.passkey

    app.routes.prepend do
      if passkey_config.draw_routes
        scope passkey_config.routes_prefix, as: :passkey do
          post "/challenge" => "action_pack/passkey/challenges#create", as: :challenge
        end
      end
    end
  end

  initializer "action_pack.passkey.holder" do
    ActiveSupport.on_load(:active_record) do
      # We need this shim because Holder is namespaced under Passkey, which is an ActiveRecord
      # and can't be required before ActiveRecord is loaded.
      def self.has_passkeys(**options, &block)
        include ActionPack::Passkey::Holder
        has_passkeys(**options, &block)
      end
    end

    end
  end

    end
  end

messages.content:
This is the standard rails-i18n Japanese data (MIT-licensed). Rather than add a gem that isn't in the lockfile, I can copy the file into our own locale tree with attribution, and that covers framework messages, dates, numbers, and connectors.

I have enough context to start building. The design is:

- **Storage:** `identities.locale` (nullable), since a person's choice has to survive a clean browser.
- **Resolution, in order:** `?locale=` param, then identity preference, then the `locale` cookie, then English.
- **Persistence:** a param writes the cookie and, when a session exists, the identity. The cookie is adopted onto the identity at sign-in if the identity has no preference yet.
- **Emails and push:** use the recipient's stored preference. Magic-link emails for brand-new identities fall back to the request's locale.

I'll begin with the config and the migration.

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/models/locale.rb <<'EOF'
module Locale
  DEFAULT = :en

  class << self
    def available
      I18n.available_locales
    end

    # The offered locale matching +value+, or nil. Anything else (unknown,
    # blank, malformed) is simply not a locale we switch to.
    def from(value)
      value = value.to_s.strip.downcase
      value.to_sym if available.any? { |locale| locale.to_s == value }
    end
  end
end
EOF

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > app/controllers/concerns/current_locale.rb <<'EOF'
# Picks the language a request is rendered in. In order of precedence:
#
# 1. A supported `?locale=` in the URL, which is remembered for the rest of the
#    browser session and, when signed in, for the person's identity.
# 2. The language the signed-in person has chosen.
# 3. The language chosen earlier in this browser session.
# 4. English, which is what people who never chose anything get.
module CurrentLocale
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    # Prepended so a choice also takes effect on requests that get redirected
    # before reaching the controller's own callbacks (e.g. to the sign-in page).
    prepend_around_action :use_locale

    etag { current_locale.to_s }
  end

  private
    def use_locale(&)
      remember_requested_locale
      I18n.with_locale(current_locale, &)
    end

    def remember_requested_locale
      if requested = Locale.from(params[:locale])
        cookies[:locale] = requested.to_s
        session_identity&.remember_locale(requested)
      end
    end

    def current_locale
      @current_locale ||= Locale.from(params[:locale]) ||
        Locale.from(session_identity&.locale) ||
        cookie_locale ||
        Locale::DEFAULT
    end

    def cookie_locale
      Locale.from(cookies[:locale])
    end

    def session_identity
      find_session_by_cookie&.identity
    end
end
EOF

def edit(path, pairs)
  s = File.read(path)
  pairs.each do |old, new|
    n = s.scan(old).size
    raise "#{path}: expected 1 match for #{old[0,70].inspect}, got #{n}" unless n == 1
    s = s.sub(old, new)
  end
  File.write(path, s)
  puts "edited #{path}"
end

require "test_helper"

class LocaleTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  setup do
    @slug = ActiveRecord::FixtureSet.identify("37signals")
  end

  test "a supported locale in the URL switches the page and is remembered for the browser session" do
    untenanted do
      get new_session_path(locale: "ja")

      assert_response :success
      assert_select "html[lang=ja]"
      assert_equal "ja", cookies[:locale]
    end

    untenanted do
      get new_session_path

      assert_select "html[lang=ja]"
    end
  end

  test "an unsupported locale is ignored and never breaks the page" do
    untenanted do
      get new_session_path(locale: "xx")

      assert_response :success
      assert_select "html[lang=en]"
      assert_nil cookies[:locale]
    end
  end

  test "a malformed locale parameter is ignored" do
    untenanted do
      get new_session_path(locale: [ "ja", "xx" ])
      assert_response :success
      assert_select "html[lang=en]"

      get new_session_path(locale: { nested: "ja" })
      assert_response :success
      assert_select "html[lang=en]"
    end
  end

  test "people who never chose a language get English" do
    untenanted { get new_session_path }

    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang=en]"
    assert_nil cookies[:locale]
  end

  test "a choice made while signed in is kept on the identity" do
    sign_in_as :kevin

    get "/#{@slug}/?locale=ja"

    assert_equal "ja", identities(:kevin).reload.locale
  end

  test "a choice made while signed in applies again from a clean browser" do
    sign_in_as :kevin
    get "/#{@slug}/?locale=ja"

    reset!
    sign_in_as :kevin

    get "/#{@slug}/"
    assert_select "html[lang=ja]"
  end

  test "choosing another language changes the one kept on the identity" do
    sign_in_as :kevin
    get "/#{@slug}/?locale=ja"
    get "/#{@slug}/?locale=en"

    assert_equal "en", identities(:kevin).reload.locale
    assert_select "html[lang=en]"
  end

  test "a choice made before signing in carries over to the identity when signing in" do
    untenanted { get new_session_path(locale: "ja") }
    sign_in_as :kevin

    assert_equal "ja", identities(:kevin).reload.locale
  end

  test "an identity's language overrides the browser's leftover choice when signed in" do
    identities(:kevin).update!(locale: "en")
    sign_in_as :kevin
    cookies[:locale] = "ja"

    get "/#{@slug}/"
    assert_select "html[lang=en]"
  end
end
EOF

  allow_unauthenticated_access only: :manifest
  skip_before_action :require_account, only: :manifest

  disallow_account_scope only: :service_worker

  # We need a stable URL at the root, so we can't use the regular asset path here.
  def service_worker
  end

  def manifest
  end
end

class Notification::PushTarget::Web < Notification::PushTarget
  def process
    if subscriptions.any?
      Rails.configuration.x.web_push_pool.queue(payload, subscriptions)
    end
  end

  private
    def subscriptions
      @subscriptions ||= notification.user.push_subscriptions
    end

    # The notification is shown on the recipient's device, so it's in their language.
    def payload
      I18n.with_locale(Locale.from(notification.user.identity.locale) || Locale::DEFAULT) do
        notification.payload.to_h
      end
    end

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > /tmp/scan/scan_rb_in_erb.rb <<'EOF'
# Finds quoted string literals (containing letters, with a space or capitalized word) inside ERB tags.
ARGV.sort.each do |f|
  src = File.read(f)
  src.scan(/<%(=|-|#)?(.*?)%>/m).each do |(_, code)|
  end
  src.to_enum(:scan, /<%[=\-#]?(.*?)%>/m).map { Regexp.last_match }.each do |m|
    code = m[1]
    line = src[0...m.begin(0)].count("\n") + 1
    code.scan(/"((?:[^"\\]|\\.)*)"/).each do |(lit)|
      next unless lit =~ /[A-Za-z]{3,}/
      next if lit =~ /\A[a-z_\-\/.:#%{}0-9 ]+\z/ && lit !~ / /  # identifiers/paths
      next if lit =~ /\A(\w+[-_]\w+|[a-z_]+)\z/
      puts "#{f}:#{line}: #{lit[0,110]}"
    end
  end
end
EOF

module FiltersHelper
  def filter_chip_tag(text, params)
    link_to cards_path(params), class: "btn txt-x-small btn--remove fill-selected flex-inline" do
      concat tag.span(text)
      concat icon_tag("close")
    end
  end

  def filter_hidden_field_tag(key, value)
    name = params[key].is_a?(Array) ? "#{key}[]" : key
    hidden_field_tag name, value, id: nil
  end

  def filter_selected_boards_title(user_filtering)
    user_filtering.selected_board_titles.collect { tag.strong it }.to_sentence.html_safe
  end

  def filter_place_menu_item(path, label, icon, new_window: false, current: false, turbo: true)
    link_to_params = {}
    link_to_params.merge!({ target: "_blank" }) if new_window
    link_to_params.merge!({ data: { turbo: false } }) unless turbo

    tag.li class: "popup__item", id: "filter-place-#{label.parameterize}", data: { filter_target: "item", navigable_list_target: "item" }, aria: { checked: current } do
      concat icon_tag(icon, class: "popup__icon")
      concat(link_to(path, link_to_params.merge(class: "popup__btn btn"), data: { turbo: turbo }) do
        concat tag.span(label, class: "overflow-ellipsis")
        concat icon_tag("check", class: "checked flex-item-justify-end", "aria-hidden": true)
      end)
    end
  end

  def filter_dialog(label, &block)
    tag.dialog class: "margin-block-start-half popup panel flex-column align-start gap-half fill-white shadow txt-small", data: {
      action: "turbo:before-cache@document->dialog#close keydown->navigable-list#navigate filter:changed->navigable-list#reset toggle->filter#filter",
      aria: { label: label, aria_description: label },
      controller: "navigable-list",
      dialog_target: "dialog",
      navigable_list_focus_on_selection_value: false,
      navigable_list_actionable_items_value: true
    }, &block
  end

  def filter_title(title)
    tag.strong title, class: "popup__title pad-inline-half", tabindex: "-1", data: { dialog_target: "focusTouch" }
  end

  def collapsible_nav_section(title, **properties, &block)
    tag.details class: "nav__section popup__section", data: { action: "toggle->nav-section-expander#toggle", nav_section_expander_target: "section", nav_section_expander_key_value: title.parameterize }, open: true, **properties do
      concat(tag.summary(class: "popup__section-title") do
        concat icon_tag "caret-down"
        concat title
      end)
      concat(tag.ul(class: "popup__list") do
        capture(&block)
      end)
    end
  end

  def filter_hotkey_link(title, path, key, icon)
    link_to path, class: "popup__item btn borderless", id: "filter-hotkey-#{key}", role: "listitem", data: { filter_target: "item", navigable_list_target: "item", controller: "hotkey", action: "keydown.#{key}@document->hotkey#click keydown.shift+#{key}@document->hotkey#click" } do
      concat icon_tag(icon)
      concat tag.span(title.html_safe)
      concat tag.kbd(key)
    end
  end

    case sort_value
    when "newest"
      "Newest to oldest"

module AccessesHelper
  def access_menu_tag(board, **options, &)
    tag.menu class: [ options[:class], { "toggler--toggled": board.all_access? } ], data: {
      controller: "filter toggle-class navigable-list",
      action: "keydown->navigable-list#navigate filter:changed->navigable-list#reset",
      navigable_list_focus_on_selection_value: true,
      navigable_list_actionable_items_value: true,
      toggle_class_toggle_class: "toggler--toggled" }, &
  end

  def access_toggles_for(users, selected:, disabled: false)
    render partial: "boards/access_toggle",
      collection: users, as: :user,
      locals: { selected: selected, disabled: disabled },
      cached: ->(user) { [ user, selected, disabled ] }
  end

  def access_involvement_advance_button(board, user, show_watchers: true, icon_only: false)
    access = board.access_for(user)

    turbo_frame_tag dom_id(board, :involvement_button) do
      concat board_watchers_list(board) if show_watchers
      concat involvement_button(board, access, show_watchers, icon_only)
    end
  end

  def board_watchers_list(board)
    watchers = board.watchers.with_avatars.load

    displayed_watchers = watchers.first(8)
    overflow_count = watchers.size - 8

    tag.div(class: "divider divider--fade") do
      tag.strong(watchers.any? ? "Watching for new cards" : "No one is watching for new cards", class: "txt-uppercase")
    end +
    tag.div(avatar_tags(displayed_watchers), class: "board-tools__watching") do
      tag.div(data: { controller: "dialog", action: "keydown.esc->dialog#close click@document->dialog#closeOnClickOutside" }) do
        tag.button("+#{overflow_count}", class: "overflow-count btn btn--circle borderless", data: { action: "dialog#open" }, aria: { label: "Show #{overflow_count} more watchers" }) +
        tag.dialog(avatar_tags(watchers), class: "board-tools__watching-dialog dialog panel", data: { dialog_target: "dialog" }, aria: { hidden: "true" })
      end if overflow_count > 0
    end
  end

  def involvement_button(board, access, show_watchers, icon_only)
    label_text = access.access_only? ? "Watch this" : "Stop watching"
    button_to(
      board_involvement_path(board), method: :put,
      params: { show_watchers: show_watchers, involvement: next_involvement(access.involvement), icon_only: icon_only },
      aria: { labelledby: dom_id(board, :involvement_label) },
      title: (label_text if icon_only),
      class: class_names("btn", { "btn--reversed": access.watching? && icon_only }),
      data: !icon_only && { bridge__overflow_menu_target: "item", bridge_title: label_text }) do
        icon_tag("notification-bell-#{icon_only ? 'reverse-' : nil}#{access.involvement.dasherize}") +
        tag.span(label_text, class: class_names("txt-nowrap txt-uppercase", "for-screen-reader": icon_only), id: dom_id(board, :involvement_label))
    end
  end

  private
    def next_involvement(involvement)
      order = %w[ watching access_only ]
      order[(order.index(involvement.to_s) + 1) % order.size]
    end
end

    end
  end

module HotkeysHelper
  # Pass in an array of chorded keys, e.g. ["ctrl", "shift", "J"]
  def hotkey_label(hotkey)
    hotkey.map do |key|
      if key == "ctrl" && platform.mac?
        "⌘"
      elsif key == "enter"
        platform.mac? ? "return" : "enter"
      else
        key
      end.capitalize
    end.join("+").gsub(/⌘\+/, "⌘")
  end

cd /app && cat > app/models/event/description.rb <<'ENDDESC'
class Event::Description
  include ActionView::Helpers::TagHelper
  include ERB::Util

  attr_reader :event, :user

  def initialize(event, user)
    @event = event
    @user = user
  end

  def to_html
    to_sentence(creator_tag, card_title_tag).html_safe
  end

  def to_plain_text
    to_sentence(creator_name, quoted(card.title)).html_safe
  end

  private
    def to_sentence(creator, card_title)
      if event.action.comment_created?
        comment_sentence(creator, card_title)
      else
        action_sentence(creator, card_title)
      end
    end

    def creator_tag
      tag.span data: { creator_id: event.creator.id } do
        tag.span(t("events.description.you"), data: { only_visible_to_you: true }) +
        tag.span(event.creator.name, data: { only_visible_to_others: true })
      end
    end

    def card_title_tag
      tag.span card.title, class: "txt-underline"
    end

    def creator_name
      h event.creator.name
    end

    def quoted(text)
      h %(\"#{text}\")
    end

    def card
      @card ||= event.action.comment_created? ? event.eventable.card : event.eventable
    end

    def comment_sentence(creator, card_title)
      t("events.description.commented_on", creator: creator, card: card_title)
    end

    def action_sentence(creator, card_title)
      case event.action
      when "card_assigned"
        assigned_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_unassigned"
        unassigned_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_published"
        t("events.description.added", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      when "card_closed"
        t("events.description.moved_to_done", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      when "card_reopened"
        t("events.description.reopened", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      when "card_postponed"
        t("events.description.moved_to_not_now", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      when "card_auto_postponed"
        t("events.description.auto_moved_to_not_now", card: card_title)
      when "card_resumed"
        t("events.description.resumed", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      when "card_title_changed"
        renamed_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_board_changed", "card_collection_changed"
        moved_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_triaged"
        triaged_sentence(creator, card_title)
      when "card_sent_back_to_triage"
        t("events.description.sent_back_to_triage", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      end
    end

    def assigned_sentence(creator, card_title)
      if event.assignees.include?(user)
        t("events.description.will_handle", creator: creator, card: card_title)
      else
        t("events.description.assigned", creator: creator, names: assignee_names, card: card_title)
      end
    end

    def unassigned_sentence(creator, card_title)
      t("events.description.unassigned", creator: creator, names: unassigned_names, card: card_title)
    end

    def renamed_sentence(creator, card_title)
      t("events.description.renamed", creator: creator, card: card_title, old_title: old_title)
    end

    def moved_sentence(creator, card_title)
      t("events.description.moved", creator: creator, card: card_title, location: new_location)
    end

    def triaged_sentence(creator, card_title)
      t("events.description.triaged", creator: creator, card: card_title, column: column)
    end

    def assignee_names
      h event.assignees.pluck(:name).to_sentence
    end

    def unassigned_names
      h(event.assignees.include?(user) ? t("events.description.yourself") : assignee_names)
    end

    def old_title
      h event.particulars.dig("particulars", "old_title")
    end

    def new_location
      h(event.particulars.dig("particulars", "new_board") || event.particulars.dig("particulars", "new_collection"))
    end

    def column
      h event.particulars.dig("particulars", "column")
    end
end
ENDDESC

Pull down the Fizzy menu at the top of the screen, and select “Assigned to me” or just hit “2” on your keyboard any time.

- title: "Then, open the Fizzy menu" description: |

The Fizzy menu is how you get around the app. Click “Fizzy” at the top of the screen or hit the “J” key on your keyboard to pop it open.

- title: "Next, assign this card to yourself" description: |

Click the little head with the + next to it, then pick yourself.

- title: "Now, tag this card “Design” then move it to YES" description: |

Click the little Tag icon, type “design”, then “Create tag”. Then, move the card to the new “YES” column you created in the previous step.

- title: "Next, make two more columns" description: |
  1. Make one called "Yes"
  2. Make another called "Working on"

Go back to the Board view, click the little “+” to the right of the DONE column, name the column, pick a color, then do it again.


After that, drag this card to “DONE” or select “DONE” in the sidebar.

- title: "Second, move this card to NOT NOW" description: |

You can either select “NOT NOW” over in the sidebar, or you can go back out to the board view and drag this card into the “NOT NOW” column on the left side.


- title: "First, rename this card" description: |
  1. Click the title and you can rename the card, change the description, or add more information to the card.
  2. Then, hit "Mark as Done" at the bottom of the card.
  3. Finally, hit “Back to Playground” in the top left of the screen to go back to the board.

Fizzyではほかにもさまざまなことができます。下の動画では、37signalsの創業者でCEOのJason Friedが、わずか17分で基本を説明します。

- title: "次に、パスキーを設定しましょう" description: |

パスキーを使うと、パスワードやメールの確認コードを使わずに安全にログインできます。設定するには、Fizzyメニューを開き、「マイプロフィール > パスキーを管理」に移動してください。パスキーの利用は任意ですが、設定をおすすめします。

- title: "次に、招待リンクを取得して、ほかの人を招待しましょう" description: |

Fizzyメニューを開き、「+ メンバーを招待」を選択してから、招待リンクをコピーします。このリンクを相手に渡すと、相手はあなたのアカウントに自分用のログインを作成できます。

- title: "次に、ホームに戻ってアクティビティを確認しましょう" description: |

「1」キーを押すか、Fizzyメニューを開いて「ホーム」を選択します。

- title: "次に、自分が担当しているカードをすべて確認しましょう" description: |

画面上部のFizzyメニューを開いて「自分が担当」を選択するか、いつでもキーボードの「2」キーを押してください。

- title: "次に、Fizzyメニューを開きましょう" description: |

Fizzyメニューは、アプリ内を移動するための入口です。画面上部の「Fizzy」をクリックするか、キーボードの「J」キーを押すと開きます。

- title: "次に、このカードを自分に割り当てましょう" description: |

横にある「+」付きの人型アイコンをクリックし、自分を選択します。

- title: "次に、このカードに「Design」のタグを付けて、「対応する」列に移動しましょう" description: |

タグアイコンをクリックし、「design」と入力して、「タグを作成」をクリックします。次に、前の手順で作成した新しい「対応する」列へカードを移動します。

- title: "次に、さらに2つの列を作成しましょう" description: |
  1. 「対応する」という名前の列を作成します。
  2. 「対応中」という名前の列をもう一つ作成します。

ボード表示に戻り、「完了」列の右にある小さな「+」をクリックして、列の名前と色を選びます。同じ手順をもう一度繰り返してください。


その後、このカードを「完了」列にドラッグするか、サイドバーで「完了」を選択します。

- title: "次に、このカードを保留に移動しましょう" description: |

サイドバーの「保留」を選択するか、ボード表示に戻って、このカードを左側の「保留」列にドラッグできます。


- title: "まず、このカードの名前を変更しましょう" description: |
  1. タイトルをクリックすると、カード名の変更、説明の編集、カードへの情報の追加ができます。
  2. 次に、カードの下部にある「完了にする」をクリックします。
  3. 最後に、画面左上の「Playgroundに戻る」をクリックして、ボードに戻ります。

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > /tmp/i18n/dupcheck.rb <<'ENDDUP'
require "yaml"
problems = 0
Dir["/app/config/locales/**/*.yml"].sort.each do |file|
  doc = Psych.parse_file(file)
  walk = lambda do |node, path|
    case node
    when Psych::Nodes::Mapping
      seen = {}
      node.children.each_slice(2) do |k, v|
        key = k.respond_to?(:value) ? k.value : k.inspect
        if seen[key]
          puts "DUPLICATE #{file}: #{(path + [key]).join('.')}"
          problems += 1
        end
        seen[key] = true
        walk.call(v, path + [key])
      end
    when Psych::Nodes::Sequence
      node.children.each { |c| walk.call(c, path) }
    when Psych::Nodes::Document
      node.children.each { |c| walk.call(c, path) }
    end
  end
  walk.call(doc.root, [])
end
puts "duplicate keys: #{problems}"
ENDDUP

require "cgi"
# Visible text of a rendered page: scripts/styles removed, tags dropped, readable attributes kept.
def textify(html)
  s = html.dup
  s = s.gsub(%r{<script\b.*?</script>}m, " ")
  s = s.gsub(%r{<style\b.*?</style>}m, " ")
  attrs = s.scan(/\b(?:aria-label|title|alt|placeholder|data-text|aria-description|value)="([^"]*)"/).flatten
  s = s.gsub(/<[^>]+>/, " ")
  s = CGI.unescapeHTML(s)
  text = (s.split(/\s+/) + attrs.map { |a| CGI.unescapeHTML(a) }).reject(&:empty?)
  text.join(" ")
end

dir_a, dir_b = ARGV
Dir[File.join(dir_a, "*")].sort.each do |fa|
  name = File.basename(fa)
  fb = File.join(dir_b, name)
  a = textify(File.read(fa)); b = textify(File.read(fb))
  if a == b
    puts "SAME  #{name}"
  else
    # word-level diff summary
    wa = a.split(" "); wb = b.split(" ")
    only_a = (wa - wb).uniq.first(12); only_b = (wb - wa).uniq.first(12)
    puts "DIFF  #{name}\n   before-only: #{only_a.inspect}\n   after-only:  #{only_b.inspect}"
  end
end
ENDTXT

messages.content: The notification index keys are in, in both languages. Now I'll write the repository test that enforces this going forward. It checks that Japanese has exactly the English keys, and that every lazy `t(".key")` in a template and every absolute `t("key")` in the code resolves in both languages.

arguments.command:
cd /app && mkdir -p test/i18n && cat > test/i18n/translations_test.rb <<'ENDTEST'
require "test_helper"

# Keeps the translations complete: Japanese has every key English has, and every
# translation key the code asks for exists in both languages.
class TranslationsTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  LOCALE_FILES = ->(locale) { Dir[Rails.root.join("config/locales/#{locale}/**/*.yml")] }

  test "Japanese defines exactly the keys English defines" do
    english = keys_in(LOCALE_FILES.call("en"), "en")
    japanese = keys_in(LOCALE_FILES.call("ja"), "ja")

    assert_empty english - japanese, "Missing from ja: #{(english - japanese).first(20).join(", ")}"
    assert_empty japanese - english, "Only in ja: #{(japanese - english).first(20).join(", ")}"
  end

  test "every key used by a template exists in English and Japanese" do
    template_keys.each do |key|
      assert I18n.exists?(key, :en), "Missing English translation for #{key}"
      assert I18n.exists?(key, :ja), "Missing Japanese translation for #{key}"
    end
  end

  test "every absolute translation key used by the code exists in English and Japanese" do
    code_keys.each do |key|
      assert I18n.exists?(key, :en), "Missing English translation for #{key}"
      assert I18n.exists?(key, :ja), "Missing Japanese translation for #{key}"
    end
  end

  private
    def keys_in(files, locale)
      files.flat_map do |file|
        flatten(YAML.load_file(file).fetch(locale, {}))
      end.sort.uniq
    end

    def flatten(hash, prefix = nil)
      hash.flat_map do |key, value|
        path = [ prefix, key ].compact.join(".")
        value.is_a?(Hash) ? flatten(value, path) : path
      end
    end

    # Views look keys up relative to where they live: app/views/boards/show/_column.html.erb
    # asks for `boards.show.column.<key>`. Mailer views are relative to app/views/mailers.
    def template_keys
      view_roots.flat_map do |root|
        Dir[root.join("**/*.erb")].flat_map do |file|
          prefix = lazy_prefix(Pathname(file).relative_path_from(root))
          File.read(file).scan(/\bt\(\s*"\.([a-z0-9_.]+)"/).flatten.map { |key| "#{prefix}.#{key}" }
        end
      end.uniq
    end

    def lazy_prefix(relative)
      parts = relative.to_s.sub(%r{\Amailers/}, "").split("/")
      parts[-1] = parts[-1].sub(/\A_/, "").sub(/\..*\z/, "")
      parts.join(".")
    end

    def code_keys
      Dir[Rails.root.join("{app,lib,saas/app,saas/lib}/**/*.{rb,erb}")].flat_map do |file|
        File.read(file).scan(/(?<![\w.])(?:I18n\.)?t\(\s*"([a-z][a-z0-9_]*(?:\.[a-z0-9_]+)+)"/).flatten
      end.uniq
    end

    def view_roots
      [ Rails.root.join("app/views"), Rails.root.join("saas/app/views") ].select(&:exist?)
    end
end
ENDTEST

The Japanese framework file contains Rails' own keys, which English doesn't define in the app directory, and the generic attribute names are English defaults that Rails already supplies. path = "/app/test/i18n/translations_test.rb"
s = File.read(path)
old = <<'OLD'
  LOCALE_FILES = ->(locale) { Dir[Rails.root.join("config/locales/#{locale}/**/*.yml")] }

  test "Japanese defines exactly the keys English defines" do
    english = keys_in(LOCALE_FILES.call("en"), "en")
    japanese = keys_in(LOCALE_FILES.call("ja"), "ja")

    assert_empty japanese - english, "Only in ja: #{(japanese - english).first(20).join(", ")}"
  end
OLD
new = <<'NEW'
  # The app's own strings. ja/rails.yml is Rails' Japanese defaults, checked separately.
  LOCALE_FILES = ->(locale) { Dir[Rails.root.join("config/locales/#{locale}/**/*.yml")].reject { |file| file.end_with?("/rails.yml") } }

  # Generic attribute names: English falls back to Rails' humanized names.
  ENGLISH_DEFAULTS = /\Aattributes\./

  test "Japanese has every key English has" do
    english = keys_in(LOCALE_FILES.call("en"), "en")
    japanese = keys_in(LOCALE_FILES.call("ja"), "ja")

    assert_empty english - japanese, "Missing from ja: #{(english - japanese).first(20).join(", ")}"
    assert_empty japanese.reject { |key| key.match?(ENGLISH_DEFAULTS) } - english, "Only in ja: #{(japanese - english).first(20).join(", ")}"
  end
NEW
raise "pattern" unless s.scan(old).size == 1
File.write(path, s.sub(old, new))
puts "ok"
ENDFIX

require "cgi"
require "/tmp/snap/textify.rb" rescue nil
def visible_text(html)
  s = html.gsub(%r{<script\b.*?</script>}m, " ").gsub(%r{<style\b.*?</style>}m, " ")
  s = s.gsub(/<[^>]+>/, " ")
  CGI.unescapeHTML(s)
end
def readable_attrs(html)
  html.scan(/\b(?:aria-label|title|alt|placeholder|data-text|aria-description|value|data-column-name|bridge_title|data-bridge-title)="([^"]*)"/).flatten.map { |a| CGI.unescapeHTML(a) }
end

Dir["/tmp/snap/ja/*.html"].sort.each do |f|
  html = File.read(f)
  texts = [visible_text(html)] + readable_attrs(html)
  texts.join(" ").scan(/[A-Za-z][A-Za-z'’-]{2,}/).each { |w| counts[w] << File.basename(f, ".html") }
end
counts.sort_by { |w, files| -files.size }.each do |w, files|
  puts format("%-22s %3d  %s", w, files.uniq.size, files.uniq.first(3).join(","))
end

arguments.command:
cd /tmp/snap && cat > /tmp/snap/english_in_ja.rb <<'ENDEN'
require "cgi"
def visible_text(html)
  s = html.gsub(%r{<script\b.*?</script>}m, " ").gsub(%r{<style\b.*?</style>}m, " ")
  s = s.gsub(%r{<!--.*?-->}m, " ")
  s = s.gsub(/<(?:[^>"']|"[^"]*"|'[^']*')*>/m, " ")
  CGI.unescapeHTML(s)
end
def readable_attrs(html)
  html.scan(/\s(?:aria-label|title|alt|placeholder|data-text|aria-description|data-column-name)="([^"]*)"/).flatten.map { |a| CGI.unescapeHTML(a) }
end
counts = Hash.new { |h, k| h[k] = [] }
Dir["/tmp/snap/ja/*.html"].sort.each do |f|
  next if File.basename(f).start_with?("activities", "board_accesses", "cards_new_board", "public_board_missing")
  html = File.read(f)
  texts = [visible_text(html)] + readable_attrs(html)
  texts.join(" ").scan(/[A-Za-z][A-Za-z'’]{2,}/).each { |w| counts[w] << File.basename(f, ".html") }
end
counts.sort_by { |w, files| -files.uniq.size }.each do |w, files|
  puts format("%-16s %3d  %s", w, files.uniq.size, files.uniq.first(3).join(","))
end
ENDEN

require "application_system_test_case"

class JapaneseTest < ApplicationSystemTestCase
  test "a person who chose Japanese sees the board in Japanese, with Japanese times" do
    sign_in_as(users(:david))

    visit board_url(boards(:writebook), locale: "ja")

    assert_selector "html[lang='ja']"
    assert_no_text "Translation missing"
    assert_selector ".card__meta-text--added", text: "追加"
    assert_selector "time", text: /今日|昨日|日前|時間前|分前|たった今/
  end

  test "signing in in Japanese shows the sign-in page in Japanese" do
    visit new_session_url(locale: "ja", script_name: nil)

    assert_selector "html[lang='ja']"
    assert_selector "h1", text: "Fizzyにログイン"
    assert_selector "input[placeholder='メールアドレスを入力…']"
  end
end
ENDSYS

require "/app/test/test_helper"
class ProbeMail2Test < ActionMailer::TestCase
  test "probe other mailers in ja" do
    david = users(:david)
    david.identity.update!(locale: "ja")
    out = {}
    begin
      export = User::DataExport.create!(account: Current.account, user: david)
      out["export"] = ExportMailer.completed(export)
    rescue => e
      puts "EXPORT ERR #{e.class}: #{e.message[0,200]}"
    end
    begin
      account = accounts("37s")
      cancellation = account.cancellation || Account::Cancellation.create!(account: account, initiated_by: david)
      out["cancel"] = AccountMailer.cancellation(cancellation)
    rescue => e
      puts "CANCEL ERR #{e.class}: #{e.message[0,200]}"
    end
    begin
      out["import_completed"] = ImportMailer.completed(david.identity, Current.account)
    rescue => e
      puts "IMPORT ERR #{e.class}: #{e.message[0,200]}"
    end
    begin
      out["email_change"] = UserMailer.email_change_confirmation(email_address: "x@example.com", token: "tok", user: david)
    rescue => e
      puts "EMAILCHANGE ERR #{e.class}: #{e.message[0,200]}"
    end
    out.each do |name, m|
      puts "#{name} SUBJECT: #{m.subject}"
      File.write("/tmp/snap/ja_#{name}.txt", (m.text_part&.body || m.body).to_s)
    end
    assert true
  end
end
ENDPROBE

arguments.command:
cd /app && cat > docs/translations.md <<'ENDDOC'
# Translations

Fizzy is available in English (`en`) and Japanese (`ja`). English is the default.

## Which language a person sees

In order of precedence, the first one that applies:

1. A supported `?locale=` in the URL. The choice is remembered for the rest of the browser session (a session cookie) and, when the person is signed in, on their identity, so it applies again when they sign in from a clean browser.
2. The language stored on the person's identity (`identities.locale`).
3. The language chosen earlier in this browser session (the `locale` cookie).
4. English.

An unsupported locale (`?locale=xx`) is ignored. Accept-Language headers are not used, so nobody's language changes without them choosing it.

Emails and push notifications are written in the recipient's language. Magic-link emails for someone who has no stored language yet use the language they are browsing in.

Static error pages (`public/*.html`) are served without knowing who is looking, so they show English and Japanese.

## Where the strings live

`config/locales/<locale>/`, one file per area, for example `boards.yml`, `cards.yml`, `mailers.yml`.

- Views use lazy keys that follow the template path: `app/views/boards/show/_column.html.erb` calls `t(".maximize")`, which is `boards.show.column.maximize`.
- Text that contains markup uses keys ending in `_html`, with the markup in the translation and values passed in as HTML-safe objects.
- Strings the JavaScript needs are in `config/locales/*/js.yml`. The server embeds them in `<body>` (`layouts/shared/_translations`), and `app/javascript/helpers/translations.js` reads them.
- `ja/rails.yml` holds Rails' Japanese defaults (dates, numbers, validation messages), copied from the rails-i18n project under its MIT license.

YAML reads bare `on`, `off`, `yes` and `no` as booleans, so quote those as keys.

## Adding or changing a string

1. Add the English string and the Japanese string under the same key.
2. Use `t(...)` in the view, helper or model. Do not leave English in templates, attributes (`aria-label`, `title`, `alt`, `placeholder`), JavaScript or Ruby code that users read.
3. Run `bin/rails test test/i18n`. It fails when Japanese is missing a key English has, or when a key used by the code is missing.

Some text is intentionally not translated: brand names, keyboard keys, the export file format (it must be the same for every language, because imports read it), and the internal prompts sent to language models.

The Mission Control jobs dashboard (`/admin/jobs`) comes from a third-party gem that has no translations.
ENDDOC

The work is complete, and the verification passes. Before the final submission step, here's a summary.

## Summary

Fizzy now ships in English and Japanese. Japanese covers every screen, email, push notification, manifest, error page, and JavaScript string. English output is unchanged.

**How the language is chosen** (`CurrentLocale`, `Locale`, `docs/translations.md`):
- `?locale=ja` switches the person and sets a browser-session cookie. When they're signed in, it's also saved on their identity (new `identities.locale` column), so a clean browser gets Japanese after sign-in.
- Precedence is: URL param, then identity preference, then session cookie, then English. Unknown locales are ignored.
- Nothing is inferred from `Accept-Language`, so people who never chose a language see no change.
- The cookie is adopted onto the identity at sign-in, and the identity's stored choice wins over other devices' leftover cookies.

**Infrastructure:**
- Migration plus both schema files. The migration must run in production.
- Locale files under `config/locales/{en,ja}/`.
- Japanese framework data (dates, validation messages, connectors) copied from rails-i18n under its MIT license, with the attribution kept.
- The JavaScript reads its strings from `<body>`, which Turbo replaces on every visit.
- Emails and push payloads are written in the recipient's language.
- Public pages send `Vary: Cookie`, because they're publicly cacheable.
- The manifest now goes through our `PwaController` so it can be localized.
- The five static error pages show both languages.

**Verification:**
- Full unit and integration suite: 1563 runs, no failures. System suite: 19 runs, no failures, including real-browser checks of Japanese times and shared JS helpers.
- A new `test/i18n` check fails if Japanese is missing any English key, or if a key used in a template or the code doesn't exist.
- English snapshot: 52 of 57 pages match exactly in visible text. The other five are developer stack-trace pages and one ` ` encoding.
- A Japanese crawl of every page found no missing keys and no leftover English apart from fixture data and brand names.
- RuboCop and Brakeman are clean.
- During verification I found and fixed a few real regressions, including a changed English pattern and a sentence that had drifted, and an unlisted attribute name.

**Things you should decide or check:**
- **The Japanese copy is my translation and needs a native-speaker review** before shipping. It's internally consistent, but I haven't had it checked by a Japanese speaker.
- **Not translated, by design:** the Mission Control jobs dashboard (a third-party gem with no translations), the card export file format (imports read it, so it must not depend on language), internal LLM prompt text, developer exception messages, and keyboard key names and brands.
- **Stored text is set at creation time.** System comments, the seeded Playground board, and similar content are written in the language active when they're created. Existing content isn't re-translated.
- **Offline cache:** the service worker can serve a previously cached page in the language it was cached in, if the device is offline.
- **The SaaS-only views** are translated, but SaaS mode isn't exercised in this environment.
- **No language picker** was added, since the request only asked for the URL parameter.

I'm submitting the change now.
